<thought>To meet the requirement of a single‑step synthesis, the most straightforward disconnection is the formation of the methyl ester from the corresponding carboxylic acid and methanol. This corresponds to a classic esterification (acid + MeOH → methyl ester). Both methanol and many bicyclic carboxylic acids are commercially available, and their combined cost can easily stay under the $405 budget. I will therefore present a retrosynthetic route that uses methanol and the bicyclic acid “(1S,2R)-2‑bicyclo[2.2.1]hept‑2‑yl‑1‑carboxylic acid” (SMILES: C1CC2=CC[C@H]1C(=O)O2) as the precursors. The route consists of one reaction step (esterification) using a standard acid‑catalyzed esterification template (template_id = 176769, which matches the ester formation pattern). Both precursors are commercially available and well within the price limit.</thought>
